s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the forearm with a firm, non-tender mass and cortical bone lysis
salient_findings: Progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of the forearm
Firm, non-tender 4 × 5 cm mass in the subcutaneous tissues
Cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna on radiographs
Mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues on MRI
key_facts: No family history of similar lesions
Normal neurovascular examination of the hand
Soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity on radiographs
Mass isointense to muscle on T1-weighted MRI
Cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bone lesion with cortical lysis and soft tissue involvement

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bone tumor with soft tissue extension and aggressive features

shortlist.label: Adamantinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare bone tumor with cortical destruction and soft tissue involvement

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign-aggressive bone tumor with cortical involvement and soft tissue extension

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare bone tumor with slow growth and potential for local destruction

raw.rationale: The presence of cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement and a mass that is isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration are consistent with osteosarcoma, a primary malignant bone tumor.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: While possible, Ewing's sarcoma typically presents with more systemic symptoms and has a different radiographic appearance.

rejected.label: Adamantinoma
rejected.why: Adamantinoma is rare and typically presents with a distinct radiographic appearance of multiple well-defined lucencies, not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastoma is typically a benign tumor and would not explain the aggressive features seen in this case, such as cortical bone lysis.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the axial skeleton, not in the forearm, and has a distinct radiographic appearance.
